      "observations": [
        "All six owned file diffs and changed test bodies were read. The patch replaces the test-settable dummy value with actual profile checks: a valid visible account with no identities or a valid identity, any enabled calendar, any address-book contact, or the startup-suppression preference makes the result false. An empty profile returns true. Accepted code separately adds the enterprise exception and excludes system address-book sources; those are later changes.",
        "Hidden accounts are filtered by the actual nsMsgAccountManager::GetAccounts receiver, whose historical IDL explicitly excludes hidden servers. The unified-folder fixture sets its server hidden. The predicate does not need a separate hidden property check. The Calendar receiver checks the disabled property of its tracked calendars; calendar-main-default in the fixture does not establish the predicate.",
        "The original browser task changes the suppression preference while the Hub is open, verifies unchanged state, closes and reopens it, then verifies not-first-run state and close-button visibility. The historical controller recomputes only in open after reset and reuses its modal, so retaining the dialog handle is not itself a stale-handle defect. Accepted source keeps the per-open state and the mid-flow stability assertions, while its browser task has later additions and a different continuation.",
        "The new xpcshell tasks directly assert empty, preference, contact, enabled-calendar, valid mail, feed, hidden-account, local-folder and invalid-server cases. They do not directly isolate a valid server with only invalid identities. Assertions in the added tasks have nonempty expected-behavior messages. One changed existing account-Hub deepEqual still has no message. The test fixture comment explains why hidden-server cleanup is skipped on debug builds; no crash was reproduced.",
        "The predicate uses early false returns and a final true fallback. Its long startup-preference comment is a local readability opportunity, not a new global comment rule. Tests register profile/calendar setup and use the existing preference harness; assertion paths and historical reports do not establish a fresh startup or UI result.",
        "B reads Parent's complete primary 2020393 description, human attachment comment, landing, activity and actual footer. The request describes first run as no accounts created, while the source deliberately also checks contacts, enabled calendars and the suppression preference. The description alone does not define the full predicate.",
        "B reads C3's full D286476 creation-to-close timeline and the actual missing-period inline 1561355. The landed setup comment ends in a period, matching the narrow request; the Done badge alone is not the adoption proof. Rebase, Try and remote-build completion remain historical records, with no fresh startup or test result. Required primary and own-review context are complete."
